AnyXboxX — Xbox Series X emulator (prototype)

 

 English · Français · Español · Deutsch · Italiano · Português · 日本語 · 中文 · Русский

 [!NOTE]
 Where we are (2026-11-25) 
 
 Measured on an i7-13700KF + RTX 4070 SUPER, Windows 11, with the VIctory fork LooperSalty/victory at commit 80d58f8 (branch anyxboxx/fork-7b0-lot9-murs ) ( third party/victory ) started by tools/lancer victory.ps1 -GameDir :
 
 - 🆕 14 fps in the world (Series X, RTX 4070 SUPER), measured 2026-11-25 : third party/victory now stands on Neptune (VIctory Edit.) 2026-11-25c with the set measured the same day (median 13.8 fps, 15.6 to 17 fps over the last minute, 72.5 ms a frame; before it, 10.9 fps median with the launcher settings of main , from automated 13-minute Series X runs, no crash). The figures below were measured with the previous base 80d58f8 .
 - 🆕 Picture-first mode, measured by the maintainer on 2026-11-25 : tools\lancer victory.ps1 -Quality (window copies read fresh each frame, smaller pools) gives clearly better lighting and textures, about 7-9 fps, and far fewer texture refusals (51-93 against about 300). The default stays the fast set (about 14-17 fps, median 13.7 over 7 minutes in the world with PR 272). -Override @{ VICTORY X = '...' } lets anyone try a setting without editing the launcher.
 - ✅ Boats float (PR 263 by Exorion1er: the ocean height maps are copied back for the title's CPU).
 - 🦀 Rust port, branch rust/full (not yet in main ) : the native launcher (PR 249) and the GPU runner anyxboxx gpu run.exe (PR 266) are now Rust; the RDNA 2 reference interpreter is ported to Rust (crate anyxboxx-rdna2-ref ) and runs every instruction the Python model runs (1,060 of the 1,490 LLVM encodings), byte for byte, with 28 parity tests; the saves, local storage, store and HDR/DXGI objects of xgameruntime are ported. Still to port: the HLSL recompiler, the rest of xgameruntime, then removing the C++ and Python. Status: docs/rust-full-status.md.
 - ⛔ Known limits (work in progress) : system RAM is the bottleneck on a 32 GB PC (the process holds about 22-25 GB: the title's own memory, plus CPU mirrors, plus VRAM spilled to shared memory), and a 12 GB card runs out of texture room (hundreds of refusals per session), which causes dips to 1-6 fps while the world streams.
 - ✅ The Xbox Series 1.0.2.1 build of GTA VI launches on PC: boot, profile screen, first-run settings, legal screens, loading, pause menu. Menus run at 30 fps.
 - ✅ It reaches the world and displays it : the character moves under the player's control and the 3D image is shown, at 4.8 to 5.4 frames per second with about 6,550 draws per frame (measured by the maintainer, Windows 11, RTX 4070 Super, VIctory log, about 4 min 20). The startup animation does not flicker (observed). The irradiance cache, never lit before (0 dispatch in a PIX capture of a cutscene frame), now has its two shade shaders translated, with their pipelines created and bound in game (observed).
 - ✅ All the cutscenes play in full (observed by the maintainer on 25 November with the launcher settings and the pinned commit 80d58f8 ), with some graphics still missing in places (the ray-tracing structure builder is off). The maintainer observed peaks at 9 fps and a steady 7 to 8 fps during the cutscenes (window caption, 25 November); in one scripted run the medians measured from the log were lower, 2 to 3 fps, depending on the scene.
 - ✅ The first two missions have been played through : a contributor of the project played for about 45 minutes at about 2 fps and completed the first two missions (reported to the maintainer on 25 November; not measured from our logs).
 - ✅ Past the prologue into chapter 1 on Linux (Jason on the boat): played on 25 November on Proton (GE-Proton11-12 with a community wineserver patch) and an AMD RX 9070 XT with the pin 890a83a , a 23-minute run without a crash, about 3 to 5 fps the whole way (VIctory log: median 3.7 fps, 80 % of the time between 2.2 and 4.5). Shadowed and indoor areas stay black (no ray tracing).
 - ⛔ Current limits: 6 shaders are still not translated (9 before), 16 pipelines are refused by the driver (the fork's issue 75 reports about 80 more on an RTX 3070, not seen on the 4070 Super), ray-traced lighting is absent (the BVH builder stays off, about 350 dispatches dropped per frame), with the VICTORY LATE WAIT setting some walls of the first room can be transparent (fork issue 168, fixes in progress: 191, 206), and long-run stability is only measured over about 4 min 20 without device loss. VICTORY RELAY is off by default: the fork's issue 89 reports that it makes the characters' skin disappear and overlaps the subtitles.
 - 👁 History of 24 November (measured or observed by the maintainer, VIctory logs): d279e69 about 4 fps, 13 min in the prison, then device lost → 7b0f736 + VICTORY RELAY=2 about 4.5 fps → launcher settings of PR 172 without DRED about 5.5 fps → batch 4 (3 pull requests) about 6.6 fps with VICTORY RELAY=2 , startup flicker fixed → this batch (7 pull requests, without VICTORY RELAY ) about 5.4 fps but 6,449 draws per frame and the best image so far → batch 8 (batch 5 plus one pull request, 11) about 4.8 to 5.4 fps, about 6,550 draws per frame, irradiance cache shaders now translated.
 - 🆕 VIctory is now copied into this repository ( third party/victory , no longer a submodule) as our own code, with nothing synced or pinned: 80d58f8 plus 57 commits for Proton (Wine) and AMD cards, from the fork fxceless/victory-fork , VIctory, klbf-lab, JoshuuDev's and myokex's victory-amd , and ours (authors in THIRD PARTY.md). Measured on Linux only (Fedora 44, RX 9070 XT, RADV, GE-Proton11-12 with a community wineserver patch, VIctory log of one run of about 23 min): about 3.7 fps (266 ms median world frame), no crash or device loss; faces, skin and geometry complete (observed); indoor and shadowed areas are black, ray tracing does not run. Not yet measured on Windows; the launcher's settings are unchanged. An existing clone must
